summary: No Forest Service page names Gladwin: it is not among the Monongahela's camping listings, nor among the developed-dispersed areas in the Forest's camping reminder (Cheat-Potomac lists Gandy Creek, Lower Glady on FR 162, and Canaan Loop Road; Lower Glady is ~7 km south-west, a different place). WVU's DIY Outdoors (a secondary listing) places it at the junction of Glady Fork and Dry Fork of the Cheat, free, first-come, no facilities. No current alert or forest order for the area. Nothing written: fees/booking left as recorded (Forest-wide free, first-come dispersed rule).
flags: No agency page at all: the Monongahela NF's camping pages and its developed-dispersed list do not mention Gladwin. The only descriptions are aggregators (The Dyrt, Campendium) and WVU's DIY Outdoors listing ('Gladwin Dispersed Camping is located at the junction of Glady Fork and Dry Fork of the Cheat River ... Dispersed campsites in the Monongahela National Forest are first come first served, there is no fee, and they do not have any facilities').

Aggregator link in website: https://thedyrt.com/camping/west-virginia/gladwin-dispersed-camping. There is no agency page for this site; the nearest official page is the Forest's camping listing https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/camping-cabins (Cheat-Potomac Ranger District, 304-257-4488 / 304-478-2000).
Missing phone: Cheat-Potomac Ranger District 304-257-4488 / 304-478-2000 (the WVU listing gives the old Cheat RD number 304-478-3251 and the Supervisor's Office 304-636-1800).

Access (aggregator only, not agency): a 2021 Campendium review says the concrete low-water bridge to the larger far-side site was mostly washed out by a flood and only small vehicles could cross; WVU warns some areas cross onto private property. AWH's note already mentions the low-water bridge and the private field. Nothing official confirms the current bridge state or that a 23-ft motorhome reaches the near-side sites.
